newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey government says Islamist curbs go ahead.
newsitem.headline: Turkey government says Islamist curbs go ahead.

text.p: Turkey's Islamist-led government has promised to go ahead with measures aimed at curbing religious activism, according to a statement issued after a crisis meeting of the country's political and army leaders.
"Agreement was reached that the cabinet will work on the co-ordinating, budgeting, planning and programming phases... of the decision," the National Security Council said.
Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist head of government, promised the crackdown two months ago.

But stalling since then by his Welfare Party has upset his conservative True Path Party coalition partners and angered military leaders, who regard themselves as the defenders of the modern, secularist tradition.
Two True Path ministers resigned earlier on Saturday because of Erbakan's reluctance to clamp down on his Islamist supporters.
True Path leader Tansu Ciller, who is the prime minister's deputy, denied a press report on Friday that she would pull out the government.

Top of the generals' list of 18 anti-Islamist demands is a call for educational reform that would require students to attend eight years of secular schooling -- rather than the current five years -- before optional Koranic training.
The army has ousted three governments since 1960 but is reluctant to stage another coup for fear of damaging Turkey's relations with the West.

The security council statement said the government had divided the anti-Islamist drive into measures to be taken over the long, short, and medium terms but gave no specific details of the cabinet's plans.

Feuding between Welfare and the army peaked last week after a middle-rank general was seen on national television calling Erbakan a "pimp" for going on pilgrimage to Mecca as the guest of Saudi Arabia's King Fahd. The Islamists threatened legal action against the general.

The army is practically the only state authority in a large chunk of south-eastern Turkey where troops are fighting Kurdish separatist rebels. Turkey also keeps some 30,000 troops on the divided island of Cyprus.
